- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean reversion or downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 2% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–4 days post-spike.
- Model consistently under-forecasts in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply a “sentiment-weighted bias” correction: add 0.3–0.8% to forecast based on sentiment average.
- If sentiment turns sharply bullish after a downtrend, model often fails to capture the momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for 2–3 days following sentiment shift.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price direction after sentiment reversal; apply a “lag correction” by adding 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment turns bullish after 2–3 days of bearish sentiment.
